question: Sonal Mansingh is an eminent Indian classical dancer and a leading exponent of Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi and _________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhau** is a semi-classical Indian dance with martial, tribal, and folk origins.
 
• It is performed during regional festivals, especially in the states of Odisha, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.
 
• The dance incorporates themes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and other Hindu mythology, as well as local folklore.
 
• Chhau dance is known for its vigorous movements and elaborate costumes, including colorful masks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• Bharatanatyam is traditionally performed by women and has its roots in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
 
• The dance form is accompanied by classical Carnatic music.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is one of the major classical dance forms of South India and originates from Andhra Pradesh.
 
• This dance is known for its graceful movements and strong narrative expression.
 
• Kuchipudi also includes the elements of dance, music, and acting, with performers often enacting stories from Hindu scriptures.
 
• It is traditionally performed by both men and women.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form from the state of Odisha in eastern India.
 
• It is known for its fluid movements, sculpturesque poses, and intricate gestures.
 
• The dance form often depicts stories from the Jagannath cult and other Hindu traditions.
 
• Odissi includes both Nritta (pure dance) and Abhinaya (expressive dance).
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**
 
 
• Sattriya is a classical dance form originating from Assam, India.
 
• It was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev as part of the religious rituals of Sattras (monasteries).
 
• Sattriya combines dance, drama, and music to depict mythological stories.
 
• This dance form is performed primarily by male monks, but it has also gained popularity among female dancers.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• Kathak is a North Indian classical dance form known for its intricate footwork and spins.
 
• The dance form evolved during the Bhakti movement and was influenced by Persian and Mughal dance forms.
 
• Kathak dancers often tell stories through their movements and expressions, accompanied by classical Hindustani music.
 
• It is traditionally performed by both men and women.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**
 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama from Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and masks.
 
• It combines dance, music, and acting to depict stories from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• Kathakali is traditionally performed by male artists, even for female roles.
 
• The dance form is characterized by its detailed facial expressions and body movements.
